prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The GNN contrastive loss uses a single global edge-weight tensor, but the *area-balance repair* then flips nodes by pure area delta, potentially undoing critical-pair co-location; by making the swap-gain prefer moving *non-critical* (low timing-weight) nodes and penalize breaking critical nets, we keep timing-critical logic co-located while still meeting area balance — reducing TNS without WNS regressions.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.715 robust(mean-std)=+0.211 min_case=+0.203 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.271 dWNS=+14.4% dTNS=+36.0% overflow~87
  bp-ng45: score=+0.203 dWNS=+9.7% dTNS=+27.5% overflow~147
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.240 dWNS=+9.4% dTNS=+34.2% overflow~132
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains (+27.5% to +36.0%) exceeding dWNS gains (+9.4% to +14.4%), consistent with the mechanism—preferring non-critical swaps preserves critical-pair co-location while area balance is still met. Overflow (~87–147) suggests some congestion cost worth monitoring. Next step: sweep the criticality penalty weight and log how many critical nets are broken per repair pass, to confirm the mechanism directly and find the TNS/overflow sweet spot.
